hypothesis: Public train count/prior residuals may distinguish independent path errors from origin/destination-correlated errors; transferable covariance assumptions can guide demand inference, while nullspace extrapolation remains an assumption.
cross_validation: Leave one corridor family (both directions) out, five folds; no evaluation count inputs used for fitting.
normalization: Prior-loaded median count scale only; independent QR-selected count equations; each covariance component normalized to mean diagonal1; each road contributes equally per dimension.
mean: One shared prior-loaded global scale correction beta, profiled GLS and clipped[-.9,2]
variance: Shared residual variance profiled on training roads only
mixture: Five nonnegative normalized covariance components, minimum weight0.0001 each; deterministic three initializations; L-BFGS-B maxiter80; training objective selects optimizer start.
evaluation: After all train CV and full-train fits freeze, report predictive count/prior-residual log density on supplied validation/private inputs for every model; no path truth, no hidden score, no model promotion.
seed: No randomness; deterministic linear algebra and optimizer initializations
caveat: Observed count covariance cannot identify arbitrary nullspace error. Counts/prior are public and previously exposed. Predictive likelihood is evidence about error assumptions only, not S_od/S_ODME. Official frozen baseline retained, no uploads.
